Write the species_flat roll-ups and the parent split

Source: R/species.R
obis_h3_write_species_flat.Rd

From the finest cell-sorted species file flat_dir/res=<from_res>.parquet (written by obis_h3_export_parquet()), writes

Usage

obis_h3_write_species_flat(
  con,
  flat_dir,
  from_res = 3L,
  res = c(1L, 2L),
  split = c(`3` = 1L),
  row_group_rows = 10000L,
  split_row_group_rows = 2048L,
  compression = "zstd"
)

Arguments

con

a DBI connection to DuckDB with the h3 extension loaded.

flat_dir

the release's species_flat/ folder.

from_res

the resolution of the file the others come from (default 3).

res

the coarser resolutions to roll up to (default 1 and 2).

split

a named integer vector, resolution = parent resolution, of the files to split (default c("3" = 1L)); NULL writes none. A split resolution must be from_res or one of res.

row_group_rows

rows per row group of the roll-ups (default 10000).

split_row_group_rows

rows per row group of the split files (default 2048, one DuckDB vector; a group holds at most twice that).

compression

Parquet codec (default "zstd").

Value

a data frame, one row per file written: path (relative to the release, species_flat/...), res, parent (NA for a roll-up), rows, bytes.

Details

  • res=<r>.parquet for each r in res (coarser than from_res): one row per cell and species, obis_h3_species_rollup_sql(), so a coarse hexagon's list is its own rows, not its children's;

  • res=<s>/p=<parent>.parquet for each s = names(split): the rows of res=<s>.parquet under one parent cell at split[[s]] (the parent's lowercase hex id), so a page reads a file small enough for its footer to come with the first range read.

Every file written has the columns cell_id, name_key, aphiaid, n, year_min, year_max (no h3: cell_id gives it, and its string statistics are the largest part of a footer), sorted by cell_id, aphiaid, in row groups of row_group_rows (the roll-ups) or split_row_group_rows (the split), so the cell_id statistics of consecutive groups ascend (a cell's rows lie in one group or in adjacent ones). As for the layer files, DuckDB writes a group of at most 2 x the size asked (v20261012's split: 4,081 rows at most for 2,048). res=<from_res>.parquet is read, never rewritten.
